Find the right hard drive for your needs by selecting your workload, capacity, and performance requirements. WD offers purpose-built storage solutions for everything from personal backup to enterprise infrastructure.
Browse WD hard drives by capacity to find the right balance of storage, performance, and cost. From everyday backup to enterprise-scale data environments, choose the capacity that fits your workload.
Internal hard drives designed for desktops, NAS systems, and surveillance environments, offering reliable performance and broad compatibility.
External and portable drives designed for plug-and-play storage, backup, and mobility across personal and professional workflows.

WD delivers high-capacity, power-efficient hard drives designed for hyperscale cloud and AI environments. These solutions help organizations store, manage, and scale massive data sets with reliability and efficiency.
High-capacity hard drives designed to maximize storage density and reduce physical footprint in large-scale data environments.
Optimized power consumption helps reduce operational costs while maintaining performance across enterprise and hyperscale deployments.
Enterprise-grade reliability designed for continuous operation in demanding environments with predictable long-term performance.
WD Red Plus and WD Red Pro are Western Digital's NAS-optimized hard drives.
WD Red Plus is ideal for home offices, small businesses, and everyday NAS workloads such as file sharing, backups, and media storage.

WD Red Pro is designed for demanding multi-user and high-density NAS environments, featuring vibration protection, NAS-optimized firmware, enterprise-class reliability, and support for workloads up to 550TB/year3.
Choose WD Red Plus for everyday NAS storage needs and WD Red Pro for heavier workloads, larger NAS systems, and business-critical applications.
WD Purple and WD Purple Pro are Western Digital's surveillance-optimized hard drives.
WD Purple is ideal for everyday surveillance systems and continuous video recording.
WD Purple Pro is designed for advanced surveillance environments with AI-enabled analytics, supporting up to 64 HD camera streams and 32 concurrent AI streams.
Choose WD Purple for standard surveillance deployments and WD Purple Pro for larger systems that require advanced analytics, higher camera densities, and smart video capabilities.

To determine the right capacity for your surveillance system, use our Surveillance Capacity Calculator to estimate storage requirements based on your camera count, resolution, recording settings, and retention goals.

An HDD stores data on spinning magnetic platters, while an SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts. SSDs are much faster for booting and loading files, while HDDs deliver far more capacity per dollar. Many systems combine an SSD for speed with an HDD for high-capacity storage and backups.
Western Digital offers several hard drives designed for RAID environments.
WD Red Plus is optimized for personal and small business NAS systems and RAID-enabled storage environments.
WD Red Pro is purpose-built for demanding NAS and RAID environments, featuring NAS-optimized firmware, vibration protection, and workloads of up to 550TB/year3.
WD Gold is designed for enterprise servers, data centers, and business-critical RAID storage environments that require maximum reliability and 24/7 operation.
The best drive depends on your workload and environment, from home and small business NAS systems to enterprise-class RAID storage.
To determine the usable storage capacity for your RAID configuration, use our RAID Storage Calculator.
Ultrastar and WD Gold drives are designed for data center environments.
Ultrastar drives are engineered for cloud, hyperscale, AI, and enterprise data centers.
WD Gold drives are built for enterprise servers, data centers, and RAID storage running demanding 24/7 workloads.
These enterprise-class drives are designed to deliver the reliability, scalability, and performance required for data center storage applications.

CMR hard drives write data tracks side by side, helping deliver consistent write performance for active workloads, NAS systems, RAID arrays, and frequent data updates. SMR hard drives overlap data tracks to increase storage density and help lower cost per terabyte, but they can be slower under sustained write workloads. For NAS and RAID environments, CMR is typically the better fit, while SMR is better suited for archival or light, read-mostly storage.

UltraSMR is Western Digital's advanced shingled magnetic recording technology used in select Ultrastar data center hard drives. It is designed to increase storage density and deliver higher capacities, enabling up to 20%+ more capacity compared to CMR-based designs while helping data centers maximize storage efficiency.

Calculate the storage required for video retention based on camera count, resolution, and recording duration.
Explore guides and resources to better understand storage technologies, use cases, and how to choose the right solution.
1MB = 1 million bytes, 1GB = 1 billion bytes, 1TB = 1 trillion bytes. Actual user capacity may be less depending on operating environment.
MTBF specifications are based on a sample population and are estimated by statistical measurements and acceleration algorithms under typical operating conditions.

Workload Rate is defined as the amount of user data transferred to or from the hard drive. Workload Rate is annualized (TB transferred × (8760 / recorded power-on hours)). Workload Rate will vary depending on your hardware and software components and configurations.
